cards.canonical_statement: In every finite-dimensional real inner-product space, for each nonzero x the vectors x and −x satisfy ‖x+(−x)‖≠‖x‖+‖−x‖. Norms are not additive in general.
cards.proof_strategy: Choose an arbitrary nonzero vector x and its opposite −x.
sketch_steps: Choose an arbitrary nonzero vector x and its opposite −x.
Their sum is zero, so the norm of that sum is zero.
Each separate norm equals the strictly positive norm of x.
The sum of the norms is therefore positive, disproving universal norm additivity in every nonzero inner-product space.
